title: Decision ledger decomposition
description: Objective: split the command-decision ledger into focused transaction, canonicalization, and replay modules. Deliverable: internal modules preserving atomic idempotent outcomes under races. NOT in scope: new command kinds, schemas, or policy. Hard dependencies: none. Owned paths: packages/store/src/decision-ledger.ts, new decision-ledger-*.ts, and command-decision tests. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/store typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/store test.
definitionOfDone: Accepted, rejected, replayed, collision, and ambiguity outcomes remain unchanged.
Concurrent duplicate and conflicting requests still yield one legal durable decision.
Every resulting production module is under 350 lines.
The focused store typecheck and test command exits 0.
taskRails: Refactor-only tasks preserve public contracts and stable errors.
Do not weaken or rewrite tests to make the split pass.
Stage only explicit owned paths; no worktree, broad add, push, or merge.

implementationPlan.description: Create `decision-ledger-canonical.ts` with its one-line `.js` bridge for deterministic request/decision materialization only. Extract narrow typed helpers that snapshot the expected-version request and decision metadata/proposal, derive request/decision/receipt/audit identities, build accepted or rejected canonical effect/result fields, construct the exact pending StoredCommandDecision/SQL bind values, and compute/finalize its decision digest. Preserve one-time hostile-byte snapshots, version constants, field order and null/empty distinctions, rejectionAuditPayload and expectedVersionConflictResultBytes bytes, PENDING_EFFECT_SHA256 compare-and-set semantics, exact stable errors, and no caller-owned mutable aliases; all database writes remain invoked inside the caller's transaction.
implementationPlan.note:
PLAN DEVIATION (recorded per epic rail + `convention-contracts-250-line-splits`): the single planned `decision-ledger-canonical.ts` measured ~303 honest lines, over the <=250 rail, so it is split at a real seam into two owned `decision-ledger-*` paths, both with one-line `.js` bridges:

Effect writes take a narrow `DecisionEffectContext` (`assertAggregateTail`, `writeCommitEffects`) so every database write is still invoked by the caller inside its own transaction.
- `decision-ledger-record.ts` (183) — canonical row persistence. Both SQL statements, `writeCanonicalDecision`, private `insertPendingDecision` / `pendingStoredDecision`, over a narrow `DecisionRecordContext { prepare }`.

implementationPlan.description: Create `decision-ledger-replay.ts` with its one-line `.js` bridge, exporting an internal DecisionReplayStore that extends DecisionReadModelStore and owns only locked historical reconciliation. Keep it protected for the transaction subclass and introduce no package-root export.
implementationPlan.note:

Therefore preserved by construction: BEGIN IMMEDIATE with `normalizeOperationalError(error, "begin replay reconciliation transaction")`; `assertDurableProjectBinding` then `loadCommandDecisionByKey`; `IdempotencyConflictError(key)` only when a historical row exists AND its `requestSha256` differs; explicit `ROLLBACK` *before* returning `toCommandDecisionResponse(historical, "REPLAYED")`; `throw missingDecisionError` when no history is found; the `isTransaction`-guarded rollback that on failure poisons and raises STORE_UNAVAILABLE "replay reconciliation could not release its read lock" with `AggregateError([error, rollbackError])`; `DurableStoreError` passthrough ahead of `normalizeOperationalError(error, "reconcile command replay")`.

implementationPlan.description: Create `decision-ledger-transaction.ts` with its one-line `.js` bridge, exporting an internal DecisionTransactionStore over the replay layer. Move commitExpectedVersionDecision while preserving exact order: open/project checks; request snapshot/scope/reserved namespace; preflight project binding + historical + aggregate tail; locked replay on history or snapshot failure; proposal precomputation only for a matching preflight version; BEGIN IMMEDIATE; authoritative binding/history/ID/receipt/tail rechecks; exactly one accepted business-effect or rejected audit receipt; canonical decision insert/digest finalize; COMMIT; and response mode. Preserve race winner behavior, SQL and effect write order, exact codes/messages, commitAttempted/isTransaction ambiguity detection, rollback aggregation, poison-on-unknown, DurableStoreError passthrough, and generic operational normalization.
implementationPlan.note:
`decision-ledger-transaction.ts` (201) + one-line `.js` bridge exports `DecisionTransactionStore extends DecisionReplayStore` with the public `commitExpectedVersionDecision`. Not exported from `index.ts`.

Order preserved exactly as specified: `requireOpen` -> PROJECT_SCOPE_REQUIRED -> `snapshotDecisionRequest` -> PROJECT_SCOPE_MISMATCH (same JSON.stringify message) -> reserved-namespace `invalidInput` -> `identifyDecisionRequest` -> `readOperation("preflight expected-version decision")` doing `assertDurableProjectBinding` + `loadCommandDecisionByKey` + `assertAggregateTail` -> preflight-history locked replay carrying the STORE_CORRUPT "disappeared between preflight and locked replay" error -> metadata snapshot with its own locked-replay catch -> `planDecision` (proposal precomputed only when preflight version matches; failure captured, not thrown) -> BEGIN IMMEDIATE -> under the lock: `assertDurableProjectBinding`, history recheck / IdempotencyConflictError, `assertDecisionNamespaceFree` (decision_id collision STORE_CORRUPT then loadReceipt DURABLE_ID_CONFLICT), `assertAggregateTail` recheck, exactly one accepted-effect OR rejected-audit branch, `writeCanonicalDecision`, COMMIT, response mode.

Ambiguity semantics kept intact: both COMMIT sites go through `commitAndRespond`, which sets `commitAttempted = true` BEFORE `exec("COMMIT")` and stays inside the try, so a COMMIT that succeeds without acknowledgement is still caught. `commitAttempted` lives on a small mutable `DecisionAttempt` holder so both call sites and the catch observe one value. `classifyDecisionFailure` computes `commitAttempted && !isTransaction` BEFORE attempting rollback, then poisons and returns OUTCOME_UNKNOWN with `AggregateError(causes)` (1 cause when rollback succeeded, 2 when it failed), then DurableStoreError passthrough, then `normalizeOperationalError(error, "commit expected-version decision")`. It returns rather than throws so the single `throw` stays at the catch site; no code path is skipped.

Subtleties handled deliberately:
- `effectContext()` is a side-effect-free closure bundle, so `lockedDecisionProposal(plan)` throwing a stored `proposalFailure` still precedes any database write.
- Accepted/rejected selection uses explicit if/else with a named `effect`, not argument-position evaluation, so effect-write ordering is not implicit.
- The colliding-ID query string is hoisted to `COLLIDING_DECISION_ID_QUERY` byte-identical to the HEAD inline literal.

Second deviation from the literal plan, same <=250 driver: `DecisionPlan`, `planDecision`, and `lockedDecisionProposal` were placed in `decision-ledger-canonical.ts` (236) rather than the transaction module. They are pure proposal materialization, which is canonical's stated job, and this leaves the transaction module holding control flow only. Without the move the transaction module landed at exactly 250 with no headroom.

`pnpm --filter @moe/store typecheck` exits 0. All four new production modules: canonical 236, record 183, replay 55, transaction 201.

implementationPlan.note:
Adversarial review of nine owned paths (plan said seven; the two extra are the <=250 canonical/record split pair recorded in steps 2 and 4). Committed as 9c87dc6.

RACE INTERLEAVINGS
- Preflight-before-winner, identical request: preflight sees no history, precomputes the proposal, then loses the lock. Under BEGIN IMMEDIATE the history recheck finds the winner, digests match, and `commitAndRespond(attempt, historical, "REPLAYED")` sets commitAttempted before COMMIT. One legal durable decision, loser replays.
- Same interleaving, conflicting request: `IdempotencyConflictError(plan.request.key)` thrown under the lock; classify sees commitAttempted false and a live transaction, rolls back cleanly, and passes the error through untouched.
- Winner-before-lock: `preflight.historical !== null` routes to `reconcileHistoricalDecision` carrying the STORE_CORRUPT "disappeared between preflight and locked replay" error, which surfaces only if the row has since vanished.

HOSTILE INPUT AND OCCUPIED IDENTITY
- `rawInput` null/non-record/malformed still fails in `snapshotDecisionRequest` after `requireOpen` and the PROJECT_SCOPE_REQUIRED guard, before any digest work.
- Reserved `targetAggregateId` returns `invalidInput` BEFORE `identifyDecisionRequest`, so INVALID_INPUT cannot be preempted by digest computation. `startsWith` keeps case-exactness.
- Hostile metadata bytes route to locked replay; hostile proposal bytes are captured into `proposalFailure` and rethrown by `lockedDecisionProposal` only when the locked version still matches — if the version moved, the rejected branch runs and the stored failure is correctly never consulted, matching HEAD.
- Caller bytes are snapshotted at most once on any path: `lockedDecisionProposal` uses `??`, so a precomputed proposal is reused rather than re-read.
- decision_id collision -> STORE_CORRUPT, then receipt occupancy -> DURABLE_ID_CONFLICT, then aggregate tail; rejection-audit occupancy -> STORE_CORRUPT before the audit payload is even built.

FAILURE AND AMBIGUITY PATHS
- Effect-write, insert, and finalize failures all raise inside the transaction try; `changes !== 1` still yields STORE_UNAVAILABLE.
- COMMIT succeeding without acknowledgement: commitAttempted true and `isTransaction` false -> poison + OUTCOME_UNKNOWN with a one-cause AggregateError. Rejected COMMIT that rolls back: `transactionEndedAfterCommitAttempt` is false, rollback succeeds, handle stays usable. Rollback failure: poison + OUTCOME_UNKNOWN with a two-cause AggregateError. The `commitAttempted && !isTransaction` value is still computed BEFORE the rollback attempt. `toCommandDecisionResponse` remains inside the try exactly as at HEAD, so post-COMMIT response failures classify identically.
- Replay digest mismatch, rollback-before-REPLAYED, and the STORE_UNAVAILABLE read-lock detail are byte-verbatim (proven in step 3).

MECHANICAL COMPARISONS VS HEAD (not eyeballed)
- String-literal set diff across HEAD `decision-ledger.ts` vs the five production files: zero real messages lost, zero added. The four reported entries were regex artifacts spanning import statements, verified individually. Every DurableStoreError code/message, `"command.expected-version-rejected"`, `"command decision position"`, and the colliding-ID query survive verbatim.
- Both SQL templates string-equal to HEAD (step 2). `reconcileHistoricalDecision` diff-clean modulo the one declared visibility change (step 3). `DecisionLedgerCore` + `createDecisionLedgerCore` diff-clean (step 5), so response freeze/copy and bound-method behavior are untouched; `validateStartup` order unchanged.
- Import graph is a strict DAG: canonical (leaf) -> record; canonical/record/replay -> transaction; transaction -> ledger; replay -> decision-read-model. No cycle. Zero references to the new internals outside the four modules, and `index.ts`, `decision-read-model.ts`, `event-ledger.ts`, `sqlite-event-store.ts` are untouched — no export, schema, or policy drift.

GATES
- Cross-platform Node line counter (CRLF/LF safe, trailing-newline safe): ledger 126, canonical 236, record 183, replay 55, transaction 201; all four `.js` bridges exactly 1. LINE-GATE PASS.
- Zero test edits: `git status --porcelain` over all store `*.test.ts`, `*test-helpers.ts`, `*.mjs` is empty.
- Regression sweep beyond the task gate: full `pnpm test` -> 62 files, 662 passed, 1 skipped.
- No debug/probe/scratch artifacts; all comparison temp files were written to `$TEMP` outside the repo and removed.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: Preserve the existing inheritance seam and turn decision-ledger.ts into a compatibility/factory facade over three focused internals: canonical record materialization, locked replay reconciliation, and the expected-version transaction. Rejected a free-standing service that duplicates DecisionReadModelStore/EventLedgerStore protected access. Rejected one generic helper because the 327-line transaction would remain unreviewable. Rejected modifying the existing large command-decision suites; they are the locked race/idempotency oracle and the refactor changes no behavior. New `.ts` internals require one-line `.js` bridges for Node strip-types runtime.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: decision-ledger.ts is 539 lines. DecisionLedgerStore extends DecisionReadModelStore, whose protected load/validation methods sit above EventLedgerStore.writeCommitEffects. The file's protected/public surface is DecisionLedgerCore, createDecisionLedgerCore, and the inherited core operations; callers do not import the concrete class. The commit flow preflights history and aggregate tail before metadata/proposal snapshotting, then rechecks every authoritative fact under BEGIN IMMEDIATE. Historical preflight and snapshot failures enter a separate locked replay reconciliation path so a concurrent winner is returned rather than lost.
planningNotes.risks: Preserve exact preflight/lock/recheck ordering, one legal winner under duplicate/conflicting processes, composite-key versus derived-ID collision errors, rejection-audit IDs/payload, receipt and decision digest versions, pending-digest finalize update, and DECIDED/REPLAYED response modes. Commit acknowledgement loss and rollback failure must poison and return OUTCOME_UNKNOWN before generic busy normalization. Canonicalization must snapshot hostile input once and never retain caller-owned bytes. No new export, command kind, schema, SQL column, or policy. Every changed/new production or test source must be <=250 physical lines; all existing tests stay byte-unchanged.

reviewSummary:
APPROVED. Commit 9c87dc6, 9 owned paths, +681/-415 (net 266). 539-line decision-ledger.ts split into 5 modules.

NOT a pure verbatim move unlike the sibling store splits - 466 -> 665 logic lines, real restructuring into narrow context interfaces. So a logic-line diff proves nothing here; the load-bearing evidence is the literal diff plus the untouched oracle suite.

LITERAL DIFF old vs the 5 new modules: ZERO error messages, SQL templates or reason codes lost. Exactly 2 deltas, both benign:
- LOST "COMMIT" x1 - HEAD had two identical call sites (155-156, 377-378), now one `commitAndRespond`. It still sets `commitAttempted = true` BEFORE `exec("COMMIT")`. That ordering IS the lost-acknowledgement invariant; inverted, every ambiguous commit would misclassify.
- ADDED "disposition" x1 - a type index, type-level only.

AMBIGUITY CLASSIFIER line-for-line vs HEAD 381-402: `commitAttempted && !isTransaction` still computed BEFORE the rollback attempt (after it, every failure would look like a lost ack), guarded rollback with own catch, 1-vs-2 cause AggregateError, poison(), same OUTCOME_UNKNOWN text and order. Only change is `throw X` -> `return X` at the call site; every path returns a value, so no `throw undefined`.

DoD2 ORACLE - untouched multi-process race suites all RUN and pass: "serializes same-key replay/conflict and same-version competing commands" (361ms, real multi-process), "reconciles a committed decision after the writer exits before an acknowledgement", plus OUTCOME_UNKNOWN and rejected-COMMIT-rollback. Zero test edits, verified in the commit AND the working tree.
